acceptance_status: Automated-inventory checkpoint; full functional/native/manual/performance/release parity remains open.
scope: Rust allocates preference outer/main/navigation/header/body/category/row/label/rule-list geometry, including centered controls, a flexible text column and native remeasurement after shrinking. Views retains the reference BoxLayouts and explicit native preferred sizes remain respected.

build_input_snapshot.gn_delta: No target/dependency change. Rust bridge adds clear_selection for existing SelectState. Explicit native adapters, preference selector allocation/refresh and browser tests changed. Concurrent root network-policy work remains excluded.
build_input_snapshot.method: Frozen UI overlay base a3afc206f742f0a59da6e65d609ddf1df3c7326d plus 16 explicit live UI overrides (including sidebar_metal.h/mm), with committed own installer/stager hooks; concurrent network-policy changes excluded. Twenty-one prototype source hashes are matched to committed, live and staged inputs.

native_service_patch.license: Generated Chromium header and source hook retain the Chromium BSD-style license; project adapter/tool/model changes use Apache-2.0.

contracts: Rust now allocates the preference root/main/navigation/header/header-text/body/category columns, all catalogue row label columns and centered row controls, plus the saved-site-rule list and centered dynamic rule rows. The native adapter supplies visibility, ignored-child flags, margins, explicit preferred sizes, native font/control measurement and the single flexible child. Views retains original BoxLayout allocation through the same adapter.

The centered allocator keeps a common cross axis with odd-size bias, asymmetric margins, signed positioning and clamped emitted extents. Shrinking preserves the initial main-axis flex budget and remeasures wrapped content. A zero/unbounded available cross extent reuses the initial natural cross measurement, matching the native fallback instead of rewrapping text at zero width.

The previous stretch allocator entry point remains unchanged in behavior and is covered by the existing tools native-BoxLayout oracle. The new center entry point is separate. Native stores, command admission, profile/global scope, deferred mutations, persistence, event/focus/AX/menu/scroll/window adapters and Rust catalogue/filter/draft/paging state remain unchanged.

Three Rust regressions cover odd/common centering with asymmetric margins, flex remeasurement and fixed controls, zero/empty/tiny constraints and saturated extents. A shared browser oracle compares actual Chromium BoxLayout preferred/minimum/height-for-width/bounded measurements and child rectangles for both orientations, three flex positions, five visibility/ignored/margin modes and 42 width/height pairs (1260 combinations).

A second shared browser oracle uses native preferred-size proxies for real controls, compares visible container layout managers and child rectangles with actual BoxLayout, and covers all ten categories and all 52 catalogue rows at compact and wide native-window sizes. It checks root/main/navigation/header/body/category, row and label allocation. Hidden navigation is checked when visible in the wide mode; the explicit external 212x1 navigation preferred size remains intact.

No dependency or browser-service policy was added. Views interaction/container identity, native scroll/viewport and window placement, responsive visibility policy, remaining header/profile/status/managed copy and full manual/performance/release acceptance remain open. No controlled CPU/GPU/presentation or memory gain is established.

initial_geometry_probe.note: The initial center allocator failed zero-cross-size remeasurement in the synthetic native oracle. The real-hierarchy oracle also incorrectly compared the navigation external explicit 212x1 preferred size to its internal allocator measurement on both backends. The adapter now uses initial natural cross size at zero/unbounded cross extent; the oracle compares layout-manager measurements, covers navigation when visible, and retains outer explicit sizes. Both original tests pass without changing the 1260-combination or ten-category/two-size coverage. Initial failed runs are retained and are not current passing results.

optional_scenarios.status: Not rerun for this presentation checkpoint. The earlier tools-chrome report retains four default-30-trial passes per backend; none is counted as a current-commit pass.
